---
title: "Missing data"
---

Suppose a vowel production study records duration and three formants for every token. The third formant tracker fails on some tokens, so the corresponding cells are blank. A blank is not a formant measurement. It records the fact that a measurement which could have been present is absent.

The reason for that absence matters. A tracker that fails independently of the formant value removes a different set of tokens from a tracker that fails on unusually high values. The visible table may not distinguish these cases because the failed measurements are precisely the values we cannot inspect.

As with [exclusion rules](../experimental-design/exclusion-rules.qmd), deleting incomplete rows changes the analyzed observations. Filling the cells also changes the data because an imputed value is an estimate produced by a rule or model, not a newly observed measurement.

## Missingness patterns and mechanisms

A [missingness pattern](missingness-patterns.qmd) records which values are absent. We represent that pattern with a missingness indicator and count absent values by row, column, and combination of columns.

A [missingness mechanism](missingness-mechanisms.qmd) is a claim about how the indicator depends on observed and unobserved measurements. This claim concerns the process that produced the missing cells. It cannot generally be read from the visible pattern alone.

## Deletion and imputation

[Complete case analysis](complete-case-analysis.qmd) deletes any row with a missing analysis variable. If the probability that a row is retained depends on the linguistic response or predictor, the complete cases represent a selected subset of the original target. When several columns contain missing values, the number of retained rows may also be much smaller than any single column's missing percentage suggests.

[**Imputation**](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-historic.html) replaces missing values with estimates produced from the observed data. [Iterative PCA imputation](pca-imputation.qmd) begins with provisional replacements, fits a low-rank representation, reconstructs the matrix, and updates the missing cells. This procedure uses the matrix factorization concepts introduced earlier. Its success depends on stable low-rank relations among the measurements.

To [validate an imputation procedure](validating-imputation.qmd), we hide some observed values, fit without access to them, and compare the imputations with their known values. This test cannot reveal the naturally missing measurements, but it can identify observed regions in which the procedure reconstructs poorly.

Any report of a missing-data analysis should distinguish the measurements that were observed, the assumptions about why other measurements were absent, the rule used to delete or impute them, and the population described by the resulting estimate.
